task: Verify that the Microbiome-CDM pipeline produces, or can produce from existing outputs, a complete, deduplicated, evidence-backed terminology catalogue over the full-text corpus.

mode_declarations.method_note: Every count was produced by an executable read-only probe over artifacts on disk using the real scripts.termpipeline.textnorm/ids helpers and the canonical section loader cdm_pipeline.ner.runner_sections.load_sections. Probe scripts are in .audit_tmp/ (scratch, not committed).

final_decision_questions.question: Do we already have a complete deduplicated terminology catalogue?
final_decision_questions.detail: A consistently deduplicated catalogue of 165991 terms exists (from 166012 rows, 21 control-byte collisions collapsed; ids re-derive exactly), but it is not complete: 94458/165991 = 56.90% of terms have no mapping row, only 838/165991 = 0.5049% have any definition, 10477/165991 = 6.31% have no mention at all, and 0/165991 are human-reviewed.

final_decision_questions.question: Can every canonical term be traced to its original mentions and source papers?
final_decision_questions.answer: Not from the artifacts as shipped
final_decision_questions.detail: canonical_term_id is null on 2505735/2505735 mention rows; the link exists only as an implicit type-constrained string join resolving 1174969/2505735 = 46.89% and losing 53.1088%. Traceability is possible in principle (occurrence_key is stable) but not materialised, and 10477 terms (6.31%) have no mention to trace to.

final_decision_questions.question: Are definitions available and traceable where they exist?
final_decision_questions.answer: Yes where they exist, but they barely exist
final_decision_questions.detail: 1150/1150 definition rows have a valid term_id, correct (term_norm, cdm_type), and a byte-exact reproducing span. Coverage is 838/165991 = 0.5049%, with 1003/1150 = 87.2% being CONTEXTUAL_DESCRIPTION rather than formal definitions, and 0 human-reviewed. No definition was fabricated for a term lacking one.

final_decision_questions.question: Are CV mappings valid, versioned where possible, and appropriately qualified?
final_decision_questions.answer: Versioned and qualified: yes; valid: unproven, with defects
final_decision_questions.detail: Vocabularies are versioned (ontology_registry.json: MeSH 2026; OMOP vocabulary_download_v5 2018-06-02; live UMLS/BioPortal/OLS4/NCBI Taxonomy) and OMOP concept ids spot-check 40/40 in the local index. RELATED_TO+AMBIGUOUS (85.08% of rows) are correctly flagged as candidates. But 5237 rows are orphans, mapping_id is not unique (3556 repeats), only 38403/334231 = 11.49% are EXACT_MATCH, and 0 are auto-accepted.

final_decision_questions.question: Are frequencies reproducible and free from cross-run double-counting?
final_decision_questions.answer: Reproducible: yes; free from cross-run double-counting: no
final_decision_questions.detail: Stored mention_count/paper_count recompute with 0 mismatches, but mention_count counts raw mention rows across four extractors, so the same span is counted up to 4x (1.8385 overall; 1.6065 on matched rows) and 23921 terms exceed their distinct-occurrence count. Section frequency is not materialised at all. Only distinct occurrence_key (1362931) is a valid occurrence unit.

final_decision_questions.question: Is the terminology resource correctly described by the broader data catalogue?
final_decision_questions.detail: data_catalogue/ documents a different artifact and never mentions results/terminology_v1/; corpus_v2/releases/2.2.0/ ships an unrelated 39694-row terminology_inventory.csv and has zero references to this build. Three inconsistent terminology inventories coexist (165991 / 166012 / 39694) with no cross-reference, and this build has no release-scoped manifest.

final_decision_questions.question: What, if anything, must be fixed before this resource can serve as the terminology layer of the Human Microbiome CDM?
final_decision_questions.detail: P1: materialise the mention-to-term link and resolve the 53.1088% type-divergent rows; fix the off-by-one declared count; de-duplicate/orphan-fix the mapping file and make mapping_id unique. P2: materialise and document section_frequency, define mention_count on distinct occurrences, add the missing catalogue fields. P3: add a discoverable checksummed catalogue/release entry and reconcile the three inventories. P4: commission human review via calibration_sample.csv. Without P3/P4 the resource remains a candidate, unvalidated terminology layer.
